review.title: The commander's qualification evidence is collected by hand, one command at a time
review.acceptance:
PW-0504 is the OBSERVATION and stays blocked on hardware. This is the PREPARATION, which is engineering, and gpt-architect's round-115 section 4 asks for it by name: 'First prepare the smallest deterministic qualification package/checklist... Prepare this so Diego's part is minimal.'

TODAY THE RUN SHEET ASKS THE COMMANDER TO TYPE POWERSHELL AND PASTE OUTPUT. Step 0 alone is three separate snippets plus two settings pages read by eye, and every later row asks him to notice and copy something. Each hand-copied field is a field that can be wrong, missing, or from the wrong machine, and 'a RIG pass on unrecorded hardware is not evidence' is this document's own rule.

REQUIRED: one command Diego runs AFTER installing and launching, which collects everything collectable without him transcribing anything -- the environment block the matrix specifies (Windows build, GPU and driver, WebView2 runtime, display, audio), the installed tree's location and whether verify-install accepts it, whether sidecar.log exists with its size and tail, whether a liberty-desktop.exe process and its node.exe child are running, and whether the handshake line is present in the log.
REQUIRED: it writes ONE file he sends back, and prints a short human summary so he can see whether it worked before sending it.
REQUIRED: ABSENCE IS RECORDED, NOT SKIPPED. A missing sidecar.log, an unresolvable WebView2 version or a process that is not running are findings the report must state explicitly -- the run sheet already says an absent log is itself a finding, and a collector that silently omitted it would undo that.
REQUIRED: IT CLAIMS NOTHING IT CANNOT SEE. It must not report that WebView2 rendered the application, that playback worked, or that the window appeared. Those are the commander's eyes and the report must say so where it would otherwise be read as covering them. gpt's round-105 section 9: do not collapse those claims.
REQUIRED: NO SECRETS. It must not capture the launch token, environment dumps, or anything from the handshake line beyond host and port.
REQUIRED: testable off Windows. Every platform fact arrives through an injected reader, the way installed-identity.mjs takes `env` as a parameter, so the composition and the absence-handling have a suite on this machine. The Windows commands themselves cannot be executed here and that limit is stated rather than glossed.
REQUIRED: the run sheet's Step 0 and its report format point at the command instead of listing snippets to retype, and the rows only a person can judge stay a person's.

OUT OF SCOPE: marking any PW-0504 row passed. This task delivers the collector; the evidence is still the commander's to produce.
review.notes:
FILED ROUND 115 under gpt-architect's instruction to minimise the commander's work before asking for it. The one-command shape is chosen because the alternative already exists and is the problem: the run sheet is correct and it is long, and length is what makes a qualification session get abbreviated.

Scope held deliberately narrow. This does not automate judgement -- G1's compositing result, G2's scaling, the SmartScreen wording, whether a window actually appeared -- only the facts a machine can read about itself.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs: 15 tests, 15 pass, 0 fail. node --check clean. repo:validate passes.

WHAT IT REPLACES. The run sheet Step 0 was three PowerShell snippets to retype plus two settings pages read by eye, and every later row asked the commander to notice and copy something. It is now one command -- node scripts\windows\qualify.mjs -- that writes one file he sends back. The matrix own rule is "a RIG pass on unrecorded hardware is not evidence", and every hand-copied field was a field that could be wrong, missing, or quietly from the wrong machine.

WHAT IT COLLECTS: the environment block the matrix specifies (Windows build, GPU and driver, WebView2 runtime, display, audio, scaling); where the application installed and whether the REAL verify-install.mjs accepts that tree; whether liberty-desktop.exe and node.exe are running; and whether sidecar.log exists, its size, whether the handshake line is present, and its tail.

IT CLAIMS NOTHING IT CANNOT SEE, and the disclaimer travels INSIDE the JSON rather than only in a covering message, because the file is what gets pasted into a thread six weeks later. Tested: the notCovered list names the window appearing, WebView2 RENDERING (a runtime version is not a render), playback, SmartScreen wording, and rows G1/G2/G3. gpt round-105 section 9 forbids collapsing those claims and this is the mechanism that keeps them apart.

ABSENCE IS A FINDING, NOT A GAP, which is the property most likely to cost a session if wrong. A reading returns {value} or {unavailable: why}, never a bare null. The WebView2 case is tested specifically because its Evergreen registry key is ABSENT whenever the runtime is per-user, which is common -- and WebView2 is the engine the entire UI runs in, so it is the single worst field to lose silently. An absent sidecar.log is recorded with the sentence that it is itself a finding. A verifier that REFUSES is recorded as a refusal rather than crashing the collector.

NO SECRETS, tested bluntly because this file gets pasted into a chat: only host and port are taken from the handshake line, never the line itself; a full report built with LIBERTY_SIDECAR_TOKEN set is asserted not to contain the token value or even the variable NAME; the log tail is bounded at 16 KiB while the true size is still reported.

MUTATION-TESTED, both properties that matter. Making a failed reading return {} instead of an absence reddens 4 cases. Echoing the whole handshake line instead of host:port reddens 1. Both reverted; 15/15 green.

STATED, NOT GLOSSED: none of the PowerShell in this file has been executed. Every reading is a Windows fact and this container is Linux; the script refuses to run off win32 with a reason rather than producing a report that would be a different thing wearing the same name. What is proven here is the composition, the absence-handling, the bounding and the redaction, all through injected readers -- the same pattern installed-identity.mjs uses with env. The first real run is the commander, and the summary it prints exists so he can see it worked before sending.

OUT OF SCOPE AND NOT DONE: no PW-0504 row is marked passed. This delivers the collector; the evidence is still the commander to produce.

recommended.title: The distribution inventory runs nowhere until the Windows workflow calls it
recommended.acceptance:
REQUIRED: the Windows package job runs scripts/windows/distribution-inventory.mjs against the PACKAGE BUILD OUTPUT after the bundle is produced, and against the INSTALLED TREE inside the lifecycle run, with each invocation naming which tree it is reporting on. Two trees, two reports, never conflated.

REQUIRED: it runs even when a later step fails, for the same reason the installer-log upload does -- the inventory of a build is most interesting on the run that went wrong.

REQUIRED: its unit suite joins npm run test:scripts, and therefore gains a step in the CI validate job, because PL-0714's mirror-check fails a build whose alias names a suite with no step. A script nothing runs is this repository's most-repeated defect and PL-0737 must not become the sixth instance.

OUT OF SCOPE: what the inventory says. This task makes it run and makes its output readable.
recommended.notes: FILED ROUND 113 alongside PL-0737, which it exists to wire in. BLOCKED BY SURFACE, not by work: .github/workflows/windows.yml is reserved by PL-0733 and package.json by PL-0728, both in gpt-architect's review queue. Same shape as PL-0736 and recorded the same way rather than worked around.

recommended.title: A task parked for an external reviewer consumes local implementation capacity
recommended.acceptance:
claude-infra's maxParallel has gone 1 -> 2 (round 109) -> 3 (round 113) -> 4 -> 5 (round 114). Every raise was justified against the same three documented conditions and every one of them held. That is the symptom, not the cause.

THE CAUSE: usageByAgent counts REVIEW toward maxParallel, and REVIEW here usually means 'parked for gpt-architect', who is not a locally executable agent. So a lane whose entire output is awaiting an EXTERNAL verdict consumes its own implementation capacity, and the only lever available is a number that was never meant to be pulled five times.

REQUIRED: a task in REVIEW whose reviewAgent is not locally executable does not count toward its owner's maxParallel. It still holds its allowedPaths -- CONFLICT DETECTION MUST NOT CHANGE, and that is the whole safety argument for the capacity limit being loosenable at all: overlap is prevented structurally by allowedPaths regardless of owner or count.
REQUIRED: 'locally executable' is read from the registry, not hard-coded to gpt-architect.
REQUIRED: a task in REVIEW with a LOCAL reviewAgent still counts, because that reviewer is real work this organisation has to do.
REQUIRED: the capacity raises this defect forced are reconsidered once it lands. If the right number for claude-infra is 2, it should go back to 2.
REQUIRED: driven by a scenario over FIXTURES, not the live board, per this suite's own standing rule, and shown to fail before the change.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing activeStatuses, which conflict detection reads. Only the capacity computation moves.
recommended.notes: FILED ROUND 114 during the release sprint, at the moment a fifth raise became the alternative to leaving PL-0734 -- item 2 on the release-impact list, directly on the launch path -- unstarted. Filed rather than fixed on the spot because scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs is reserved by PL-0735 in review, and because a control-plane change made in a hurry during a release sprint is how a scheduler quietly starts producing different waves.

recommended.title: test:scripts and the CI validate job can disagree in one direction without anything noticing
recommended.acceptance:
FILED ON A FALSE PREMISE AND REWRITTEN BEFORE ANY WORK. The original said apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs "is run by nothing" and called it the fifth instance of a suite no gate asks. IT RUNS IN CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml, validate job, step id `notices-suite`, `node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs`, added by PL-0714. The claim came from reading that file's own header comment -- "NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY RUNS THIS FILE AUTOMATICALLY YET" -- which was true when PW-0208 wrote it and was made false by PL-0714 a round later. The correction is recorded as a defect.found event.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND IT IS SMALLER AND MORE INTERESTING.

1. THE SUITE IS NOT IN `npm run test:scripts`, so it is not in `npm run check` either. It runs on every push and never on a developer's machine through the command this repository tells people to run. That is a coverage asymmetry, not an absence.

2. PL-0714's `mirror-check` CANNOT DETECT THAT, and this is the finding worth the task. It derives the alias's scripts from package.json, derives the job's from the workflow, and fails when a script in the ALIAS has no STEP. The reverse -- a step with no alias entry -- is not checked in either direction. Measured: adding notices.test.mjs to the alias makes the check report "every suite in the alias has a step in this job" and exit 0, and removing it again also exits 0. The mechanism PL-0714 built to end a hand-kept list is itself one-directional, so half the drift it was built for is still invisible.

REQUIRED: `npm run test:scripts` names the suite, so `npm run check` covers it locally.
REQUIRED: the mirror check becomes BIDIRECTIONAL -- a suite step in the validate job with no entry in the alias fails too, with the same kind of message. PL-0714's own words apply: "the note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step did not keep it in step on any of the three occasions", and a one-directional check is half a note.
REQUIRED: both directions are proven to FAIL, by removing an entry from each side in turn and showing the check goes red, not merely by showing it green today.
REQUIRED: the stale header comment in notices.test.mjs is corrected, because it is what produced the false premise above. A comment that outlives the code it describes is the failure this project keeps recording.

OUT OF SCOPE: making apps/desktop an npm workspace. Round 106 measured that and it breaks repo:validate; the account is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.
recommended.notes:
FILED ROUND 111 by claude-infra during PW-0208, ON A FALSE PREMISE, and rewritten the same round by claude-lead after checking the workflow rather than trusting a comment. Surface widened from package.json alone to include ci.yml (the mirror check lives there) and notices.test.mjs (its header carries the stale claim). Priority dropped P2 -> P3: a local-coverage gap and a one-directional check, not a suite running nowhere.

COLLIDES WITH: .github/workflows/ci.yml is PL-0717's (REVIEW) and PL-0726's (REVIEW) surface, so this cannot be active beside either. That is why it is not being executed now.
